The course covers how satellite imagery, aerial photographs and mapping software are used to find, map and monitor sites. Each live session is recorded for participants who miss it.

The course is run for your batch on dates you choose. Timings, pace and assessment are agreed before it begins.

What it covers

  • Satellite images and aerial photographs as sources
  • Using mapping software to find and map sites
  • Monitoring how a site changes over time
  • Live weekend sessions, with recordings of each

Course outline

  1. Remote sensing basics

    Spectral imagery, visibility, ground truth.

    You: study known site

  2. GIS skills

    Georeferencing and points/polygons.

    You: create map

  3. Interpretation

    Historic maps and land-use change.

    You: critical overlay

  4. Ethics and submission

    Sensitive site coordinates and claims.

    You: final map with metadata

  5. Remote sensing practice

    Compare historic imagery and land-cover change at known documented sites.

    You: image comparison

  6. GIS field records

    Create and check structured site inventory and metadata.

    You: GIS table

  7. Critical interpretation

    Recognise false positives and the need for ground verification.

    You: uncertainty map

  8. Capstone review

    Present maps with provenance and culturally sensitive location masking.

    You: map and short report

The number and length of sessions are agreed with your batch.

By the end you can

  • Use satellite images and aerial photographs as sources for finding and studying sites.
  • Georeference imagery and map sites with points and polygons in mapping software.
  • Recognise false positives in imagery and explain why ground verification is needed.

You take away

A portfolio of your work from each session.
